_provenance.paper: A. Airapetian et al. (HERMES Collaboration), 'Inclusive measurements of inelastic electron and positron scattering from unpolarized hydrogen and deuterium targets', JHEP 05 (2011) 126, doi:10.1007/JHEP05(2011)126, arXiv:1103.5704 (read: PolarizedLithiumSim/refs/1103.5704.pdf)
_provenance.publishing_convention: F2 PER NUCLEON: the paper normalises every cross section to 'the integrated luminosity L per nucleon' (its Eq. (4.3), with the factor A/Z), so F2d is the deuteron's F2 per nucleon (0.036-0.354 over the table, about 0.33 at x ~ 0.1: the size of one nucleon's F2, as NMC's F2d), not per deuteron. F2 'is derived using the parameterization R = R1998' (Tables 5, 6 captions; sec. 4). <x>, <Q2> are the bin averages.
_provenance.errors: In PERCENT of the value: stat, and the systematics PID (particle identification), MOD (model dependence outside the acceptance), MIS (misalignment), RAD (Bethe-Heitler efficiencies) -- per bin; plus an OVERALL normalisation uncertainty, 7.6 % (proton) and 7.5 % (deuteron), 'dominated by the uncertainty of the year-dependent luminosity constant' (sec. 5.1), i.e. common to every bin of a target (body.<target>.norm_pct). No covariance matrix is given.
_provenance.cross_check: all 81 rows of each target (bin numbers, <x>, <Q2>, F2 and the five per-bin uncertainty columns) equal the paper's Tables 5 (p) and 6 (d) as printed (arXiv:1103.5704 pp. 30-34), checked by machine against pdftotext of the paper when this file was written
_provenance.record_defect: RECORD DEFECT (found 2026-10-26, not used here): the d2sigma/dxdQ2 column of Table 2 (deuteron) is identical to Table 1's (proton) in all 81 rows (checked) and matches the paper's PROTON Table 5 in 81 of 81 rows, its DEUTERON Table 6 in 1; the F2(DEUT) column and every uncertainty column agree with the paper's Table 6 in all 81 rows. Only F2 is vendored.
_provenance.in_r1998_fit: NO (published 2011); and the F2 values themselves were derived with R = R1998.

The harness that reads this file re-checks the sha256 of every byte of it, and of the canonical body (json.dumps(body, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=True)) recorded as `_body_sha256`, on every read.
